ATTRIBUTION_GAP: NavierStokes.ActualCandidateAssembly.stages_smooth (ActualCandidateAssembly.lean:879) states smoothness of the stages, not of the prefixes; NavierStokes.MixedDiagonalResidual.uncutVelocity_smooth (MixedDiagonalResidual.lean:72) is the generic prefix step; no 'ContDiffOn ℝ ∞ (DiagonalJetBounds.uncutPrefix …)' declaration exists for the pressure prefix at qbig B N0.

Both substantive clauses are accounted for. The common-domain clause is stated in Lean, with q_big = qbig B N0 > 0 depending only on the construction data and the smoothness holding at order ∞ on the one sublevel set {0 < q < q_big}; the prefix version is a three-line conjunction of stages_smooth, physicalDomain_open and uncutVelocity_smooth, so the gap is packaging, not mathematics. 'Well defined' is necessarily re-expressed as C^∞ smoothness, since Lean fields are total — an encoding choice that is stronger, not weaker. The derivative-budget clause has no formalisation, but C^∞ regularity makes the count unnecessary rather than unproved. Stage-dependent constants are explicit. Hence different_formulation, SINGLE_SOURCE_OK, three low findings.

findings.summary: 'Well defined on 0 < q < q_big' has no literal counterpart: Lean fields are total functions, so definedness is encoded as C^∞ smoothness on the sublevel set physicalSublevel h (qbig B N0) = preterminal ∩ {physicalQ < qbig}.

The second clause — the finite input-derivative budget, proved on p. 112 by the DAG recursion D_{v,a}(m) = max_{w→v} D_{w,a}(m+d_{v,w}) — has no formal counterpart; no declaration was found that counts derivatives of inputs.

No single declaration says 'the actual construction's finite partial sums are smooth on one common 0 < q < q_big'. It is stages_smooth plus physicalDomain_open plus the generic uncutVelocity_smooth, with the pressure prefix needing a ContDiffOn.sum step that no declaration records.
